analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 11.16.26
key_insights: Futures lower to start the week (Nasdaq -120bps, S&P -50bps, Russell -50bps) as global tech and AI assets fall again. In the US: NVDA -3.5%, DRAM -6%, SMH -3%, Neoclouds -7%. Globally: Korea -3.6%, Japan -2.4%, Euro Tech -0.65%.

Markets are absorbing the implications of Jensen Huang's departure from NVDA for the AI ecosystem. Huang resigned over reports of affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate. An independent board probe is under way.

FT reports Huang is discussing a comeback as NVDA CEO. Allies are assembling a 'war room' of Silicon Valley executives and would seek White House support. Bessent urged NVDA to pursue a 'dramatic' shakeup and look externally for its next CEO (BBG).

FT reports Congress is moving to pass tighter AI chip export rules after the NVDA scandal. Both parties back bills curbing sales of sensitive chips to China and giving Congress the ability to review and potentially block sales already approved by the Trump administration.
Other single-stock moves: SPCX flat after the successful Starship catch, BABA -2% on a new Qwen model, TTWO +2.5% on GTA VI anticipation (reports of strong pre-orders).

AAPL is betting on Siri AI app integrations as the main draw for its smart glasses (Bloomberg). Controls for Apple's own apps are planned for iOS 27.3 in December, outside app support comes later, and Apple still aims to introduce the glasses at its June 2027 developer conference.

GS (Sheridan) says Starship Flight 15 (11/13-11/14) and the first tower catch of the spacecraft on 11/14 are positive proof points for reusability, which it believes becomes 'somewhat de-risked'. Engine performance improved vs Flight 14, Ship 42 stayed in orbit about 22h over 14 orbits (the longest Starship flight), and 26 Starlink V3 satellites were deployed. Each of the last 2 Starship flights carried about 10 Falcon 9 launches' worth of capacity.

Callahan: NDX broke a 4-week losing streak, closing up about 350bps on the week, led by SOX up about 800bps (best week since early August). Both NDX and SOX still closed below their 200-day moving averages on Friday. NVDA is down 12% YTD after its biggest week of underperformance vs semis since 2008.

US financial conditions are at their tightest in about 18 months after another hot CPI print. 10Y yield is back at 5.15% and oil near $96/bbl. Callahan attributes last week's strength mostly to cleaner positioning (GS PB data shows covering via macro products) and rotations into defensives, big tech (including AMD and AVGO) and low-vol names.

Callahan sees relatively little consensus in the market, apart from a receptive tilt toward hyperscalers. Debate centres on where the AI/semi cycle stands, what is priced in, and whether this is a bear market bounce or a forming bull market. Software dispersion is rising, Internet is squeezy and hard to trade, and some value interest is emerging. He calls this a 'blank slate' on positioning and sentiment and a healthier landscape into 2027.

Macro this morning: SPX futures -35bps, NDX -90bps, RTY -35bps, UST 10Y unchanged at 5.135%, WTI -60bps at $88. Pre-market: NVDA -2.6%, DRAM -5%, SMH -3%, Neoclouds -6%, Tokyo Electron -7%, Hynix -7.8%, TSMC -5.7%. There is no single catalyst. Focus is on NVDA ex-Jensen (capex cycle duration, NVDA's financial support for Neoclouds, possible export rule changes), with the NVDA EPS print on Tuesday.

China's October retail sales and industrial production both missed, as did Japan's Q3 GDP. Iran targeted a US air defense radar at a base in Bahrain with drones for the second time in three days, ahead of Trump's meetings with Xi and Putin at the APEC sidelines this week (BBG).

GS Prime Services: S&P 500 gained +2.5% on the week. Hedge funds net sold US equities for a 2nd straight week (5 of the last 6), driven by single-stock short sales partly offset by macro-product short covers and long buys. US ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest % covering in 7 months. 8 of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Financials, Healthcare and Staples. Net selling in US Financials was the largest in 8 months (99th percentile on a 5-year lookback).

Prime flows: long-only and hedge fund clients were both moderate net sellers. There was heavy NVDA supply from long-only clients, rotated into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech. Memory, IPPs and Datacenters outperformed on the week. Quantum Computing, Goldminers and Memes underperformed.

Futures: Russell 2000 funding richened significantly on Nov 11, suggesting demand for leveraged long exposure from the Other and Non-Reportable cohorts, a small part of open interest. An extended rate hiking cycle remains an imminent threat. Earlier in 2026, Asset Manager gross longs were strongly correlated with SOFR, and they liquidated Russell 2000 futures when the market priced higher-for-longer rates.

Derivatives: US L/S net leverage is near 5-year lows, the Panic Index is 6.5/10, and index skew is bid, allowing costless collars. Nov 5 was the largest put volume session ever. Last week was one of the most volatile 'average stock' periods since March 2020. VIX puts traded more volume over the last 10 sessions than at any other point this year, reflecting more confidence in 'vol lower' than in 'spot higher'.

Baskets: the momentum regime shift that began this summer is re-emerging. 12m Momentum (GSPRHIMO) had its best outperformance day on record vs 3m and 6m Momentum on Wednesday. AI names are moving into the short legs of 3m and 6m momentum. Momentum positioning has collapsed and the consensus winners are no longer crowded. GS flags tactical shorts in former 12m momentum short names, or broadening into lower-quality software and staples where fundamentals have not supported the rally.

GS research on China Internet and AI models: tighter US rules on rented and remote compute access (and KYC) would likely limit China's AI labs from training frontier models at maximum scale, while application deployment and inference should stay largely resilient using domestic chips. GS expects a bifurcated AI development path and a wider frontier capability gap, with Chinese players pivoting to enterprise and industrial solutions, inference cost optimization, open-weight distribution, multimodal and embodied AI. GS takes no view on the final policy outcome.

GS reiterates Buy on SPGI after a non-deal roadshow. The contemplated CapIQ separation leaves RemainCo centred on Ratings, Indices and Energy. Indices gain from the renewed CBOE agreement (a couple of points of growth in 2027 plus take-rate increases) and from prediction markets and tokenization. Energy should return to 6-8% growth in 2027. GS sees mid-to-high single-digit organic revenue growth, margin expansion and mid-teens EPS growth.
Street upgrades: ABNB (Neutral, Phillip Capital), BILL (Market Perform, William Blair).

Event calendar: Mon 11/16 Fed Chair Warsh speech at 1pm ET and China retail sales. Tue 11/17 US retail sales, NVDA earnings after the close, MSFT Ignite keynote at 1pm ET. Wed 11/18 FOMC minutes, PANW earnings after the close. Thu 11/19 BABA, Walmart, PDD earnings pre-market and the GTA VI launch (TTWO).

sector_views.rationale: SOX rose about 800bps last week but closed below its 200-day average. Markets are debating the AI/semi cycle and NVDA's leadership risk, and momentum is rotating away from AI names.
Dispersion has increased, including within Cyber and Data Infra. GS flags lower-quality software as a possible broadening trade where fundamentals have not supported the rally.
Trading is squeezy and difficult, with some value interest emerging.
A tighter compute-access regime would limit frontier training, while inference and applications should remain resilient on domestic chips.

earnings_insights: NVDA reports on Tuesday 11/17 after the close. The report gives no EPS or revenue estimates.

Week-ahead earnings: BIDU, HTHT, IQ and XPEV pre-market Monday. DIS, JD and TME pre-market Tuesday. Tencent pre-market Wednesday, PANW after the close. BABA, Walmart and PDD pre-market Thursday, INTU after the close. Consumer prints: TSN and ARMK Mon, HD Tue, TJX, TGT and LOW Wed, WMT, ROST and GAP Thu, BJ Fri.
SPGI: GS expects mid-teens EPS growth and Energy growth of 6-8% in 2027. These are GS forecasts, not reported figures.

tension_points.bull_case: Last week's rebound came with cleaner positioning and rotation into hyperscalers, AMD, AVGO and defensives. SOX rose about 800bps. Momentum positioning has collapsed and the consensus winners are no longer crowded, and GS calls the lack of consensus a healthier backdrop into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: NDX and SOX still closed below their 200-day averages. NVDA's leadership crisis, possible tighter export rules, hot CPI, a 10Y near 5.15% and tight financial conditions weigh on the trade. Hedge funds were net sellers and long-only clients sold NVDA.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot-print or guide-down reaction in NVDA earnings on Tuesday, or a resumption of the momentum rotation against AI names.
